title: Well-definedness of right derived functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives, let
$v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive] functor, and let
$X$ be an object of $\mathcal A$ (for instance of a Grothendieck abelian category
[def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], such as $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_T)$ for a ringed space $(T,\mathcal O_T)$). Then $R^nv(X)$ is well defined, independent of
the chosen injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and
$R^0v(X)\cong v(X)$ naturally in $X$.
